findings.title: retryCount deletion branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This SMS cron will therefore delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) whose retryCount exceeds 1. Today only this handler increments the field, but retryCount is a shared column on WorkflowReminder. Once the email or WhatsApp schedulers start using it with their own retry policy, this job will silently delete their reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to that branch.

findings.title: Unguarded DB update inside catch can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` in the `catch` block is not wrapped in its own try/catch. It can throw, for example if the record was deleted concurrently because the booking was cancelled or rescheduled, or on a transient DB error. If it does, the exception escapes the for-loop and the handler. All remaining reminders in that batch go unprocessed and the cron returns an error. The same applies to the retry-increment update in the `else` branch. Wrap the increment so a failure there only logs.

findings.title: Reminders with no sendTo or empty message are never counted as failures
findings.body: retryCount is only incremented when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy or throws. If `sendTo` is missing (e.g. no smsReminderNumber) or the generated message is empty, the reminder is skipped without incrementing. The same happens for reminders skipped by the `!reminder.workflowStep || !reminder.booking` check. These reminders keep being re-fetched every cron run until their scheduled date, which is the exact behaviour this PR is meant to stop.

findings.title: Non-atomic retryCount increment
findings.body: The new count is computed as `reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value read at fetch time. If two cron invocations overlap, increments can be lost. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` instead.
